speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are presenting with a chronic cough and recurrent bouts of bronchitis. To better understand your condition, I need to ask you a few questions. How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and do they occur at any specific time of day or season?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old woman. The patient has been experiencing an aggressive cough producing copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for about 11 years, with exacerbations similar to the current presentation today. Reports that the cough is worse in the morning and has had multiple evaluations in the past due to recurrent bouts of bronchitis requiring antibiotics treatment. The patient is a non-smoker.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Bronchiectasis. The combination of a chronic cough producing copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for 11 years, with recurrent exacerbations requiring antibiotics, is highly characteristic of bronchiectasis. I request a CT Chest to confirm the diagnosis.
